result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO TO CONTROLLER - March 2026 Revenue Recognition: Dunmore Foods and Harlow Freight (US entity)
Prepared by: Senior Accountant, 2026-04-03

SUMMARY OF ENTRIES POSTED (both USD, dated 2026-03-31, both below the USD 10,000 approval threshold - no approval request required; support attached to each)

1) JE-00311 - Dunmore Foods rev rec March 2026: Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue 5,000.00 / Cr 4000 Subscription Revenue 5,000.00
   Support: DOC-0002 (Subscription Agreement), DOC-0155 (Amendment No. 1), DOC-0156 (INV-1052), DOC-0005 (INV-1001)
2) JE-00312 - Harlow Freight usage revenue March 2026 (unbilled): Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables 5,000.00 / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue 5,000.00
   Support: DOC-0001 (Usage Agreement), DOC-0206 (March usage report)

DUNMORE FOODS - ASC 606 ANALYSIS
Facts: Original contract (DOC-0002) - core platform subscription, 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, USD 48,000/yr invoiced annually in advance (INV-1001, JE-00012 deferred to 2200, cash received JE-00079). Service provided evenly over the term; Jan and Feb recognized at 4,000/month (JE-00111, JE-00215). Amendment No. 1 (DOC-0155), effective 2026-03-01, adds the Analytics module for 2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31 at USD 1,000/month (USD 10,000 total), invoiced in advance on INV-1052 (DOC-0156; JE-00229 booked Dr 1100 / Cr 2200 10,000). The amendment states the Analytics module is a distinct service priced at its standalone selling price and that core subscription terms are unchanged.
Conclusion - contract modification treated as a SEPARATE CONTRACT (ASC 606-10-25-12): both criteria are met - (a) the scope increases by the addition of a promised service that is distinct, and (b) the price increases by an amount reflecting the standalone selling price of the added service. Therefore there is no reallocation of the transaction price to the core subscription and no cumulative catch-up; the existing core contract continues to be recognized at 4,000/month, and the Analytics module is a new stand-ready performance obligation satisfied over time (ratably, ASC 606-10-55-16/25-27) over its 10-month term.
March 2026 revenue: Core 48,000 / 12 = 4,000.00; Analytics 10,000 / 10 months (Mar-Dec) = 1,000.00; Total 5,000.00.
Deferred revenue roll-forward (2200, US - entirely Dunmore): Opening Mar 40,000 (48,000 - 8,000 recognized Jan/Feb) + 10,000 INV-1052 - 5,000 March recognition = 45,000 closing. Ties to GL: 2200 ending balance USD 45,000 credit. Remaining to be recognized Apr-Dec: core 36,000 (9 x 4,000) + Analytics 9,000 (9 x 1,000) = 45,000. Agrees.
SLA credits (policy sec. 7): searched the document store for uptime reports/SLA credits for March - none exist for Dunmore, so no revenue reduction is warranted.

HARLOW FREIGHT - ASC 606 ANALYSIS
Facts: Usage agreement (DOC-0001) - USD 0.10 per shipment processed, no minimum, invoiced quarterly in arrears (Q1 invoice to be issued early April). The contract states Halvard's performance obligation is satisfied as each shipment is processed. March usage report (DOC-0206): 50,000 shipments.
Conclusion: This is a series of distinct services satisfied over time with usage-based variable consideration; under ASC 606-10-32-40 / 55-65 and the 'as-invoiced' practical expedient logic (606-10-55-18), the usage-based fee is allocated to the period in which the usage occurs. Revenue is recognized in March for March shipments regardless of the April billing date. Because the amount is earned but not yet invoiced, policy sec. 6 requires it to be recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
March 2026 revenue: 50,000 x 0.10 = 5,000.00.
Unbilled receivable roll-forward (1300, US - entirely Harlow): Jan 4,120 (JE-00112, 41,200 shipments) + Feb 4,480 (JE-00210, 44,800 shipments) + Mar 5,000 (JE-00312) = 13,600. Ties to GL: 1300 ending balance USD 13,600 debit. This full Q1 balance should be reclassified to 1100 Accounts Receivable when the Q1 invoice (USD 13,600) is issued in April.

OTHER CHECKS PERFORMED
- Confirmed no March revenue recognition entries already existed for either customer (no duplicate risk); 4100 had zero March activity before posting; 4000 March activity consisted only of monthly-billed customers (Beacon Health, Fairview Labs, Acme Logistics, Corvid Retail, Evergreen Bank) recognized directly on invoice.
- Both entries are single transactions per customer at USD 5,000 each; no splitting to avoid the approval threshold.
- US checklist item 'Revenue recognition' marked complete: the 2200 and 1300 balances are fully explained by Dunmore and Harlow respectively, and all other March US revenue is billed monthly and already in 4000.

EXCEPTIONS: None flagged. All amounts fully supported by contract terms, invoices and usage reports.

FOLLOW-UP FOR APRIL: (1) Issue Harlow Freight Q1 invoice for USD 13,600 (140,000 shipments x 0.10) and reclass 1300 to 1100. (2) Continue Dunmore at 5,000/month (4,000 core + 1,000 Analytics) through December 2026.
